# The `skill` kind

a skill reaches context in two steps: its `description` is listed from session start, and its body loads only when the skill is invoked — by `/name`, or by Claude matching the description — so the description carries the trigger and the body the procedure. A `paths` list withholds even the listing until Read, Write or Edit touches a matching file, and supporting files load only when the body sends Claude to one. Set `disable-model-invocation: true` for side-effectful workflows you want to time yourself — it drops the description from context too, so only `/name` loads the skill; `user-invocable: false` for background knowledge that is not a command. Prefer gerund or noun-phrase names (`processing-pdfs`, `pdf-processing`) over vague ones (`helper`, `utils`); `metadata` is the sanctioned home for versioning — there is no top-level `version` field.

## Locus

Each member is its own document, at:

- `**/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`

## Clauses

- `required` on `name` (required): Every skill declares a `name` — the slug the harness binds to. Claude Code alone would default it from the directory name, but a nameless skill is not portable: the spec and Anthropic's upload validation both require it.
- `min_len` on `name` (required): A present-but-empty name fails the spec's 1-64 character bound.
- `allowed_chars` on `name` (required): Lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens only — `PDF-Processing` is the spec's own counter-example. The charset also keeps XML out of the name, which Anthropic's upload validation separately forbids.
- `max_len` on `name` (required): Keep the name short and slug-like; it becomes a directory and an id.
- `shape` on `name` (required): A hyphen separates segments, so it may not lead, trail, or double — `-pdf`, `pdf-`, and `pdf--processing` are the spec's own counter-examples. The charset clause above admits the hyphen; this places it.
- `deny` on `name` (required): Reserved words, enforced by Anthropic's platform upload validation (not by the open spec, and not by Claude Code's runtime — which itself ships a `claude-api` skill). Keep them out if the skill will ever travel through the API or claude.ai.
- `name-matches-dir` (required): The spec requires the name to match its parent directory. Claude Code decouples the two (the frontmatter name is a display label; the directory names the slash command, except for a plugin-root SKILL.md) — but a mismatch is a portability trap and a reader trap even where it loads.
- `required` on `description` (required): The description is how the model chooses this skill from potentially 100+ available — it is the skill's API. Claude Code would fall back to the body's first paragraph; the spec and upload validation require it declared.
- `min_len` on `description` (required): Say both what the skill does and when to use it, with the keywords a user would naturally say. Write in third person — the text is injected into the system prompt, and inconsistent point-of-view causes discovery problems.
- `max_len` on `description` (required): The spec's cap. Claude Code additionally truncates the skill listing at 1,536 combined characters (description + when_to_use) — truncation, not rejection, but text past the fold cannot help the model choose.
- `shape` on `description` (required): Anthropic's platform upload validation rejects a description carrying an XML tag — the description is injected into the system prompt, where a tag is markup rather than text. Neither the open spec nor Claude Code's runtime enforces it, so this is the clause that keeps a skill portable through the API and claude.ai. Prose spelling a comparison (`use when x < y`) is not a tag and does not fire.
- `max_len` on `compatibility` (required): Optional field; when present the spec caps it at 500 characters. Most skills do not need it.
- `extent` (advisory): Progressive disclosure: keep SKILL.md under 500 rendered lines and move detailed reference material to separate files, one level deep. Measured render-side — the lines the projected artifact contributes to context, not the source body before any include resolves. Once a skill loads, its body stays in context across turns — every line is a recurring token cost. The context window is a public good.
- `forbidden_keys` (required): Cursor `.mdc` keys. Nothing in the Agent Skills spec or Claude Code's documented frontmatter accepts them — a skill authored with them is carrying dead configuration that another tool's semantics silently fail to apply.
- `glob-valid` on `paths` (required): The optional `paths` scope gates every invocation channel until a file tool (read, edit, write) touches a path its globs match; each entry is a glob (brace expansion supported). An unparseable pattern — an unclosed `[`, say — is invalid under globset and silently matches nothing, so the gate never opens and the skill never registers, with no error surfaced. Fix the pattern or drop the field.
- `mention-reachable` on `paths` (advisory): A mention of a gated member is actionable only where that member can be invoked. A `paths` gate removes its member from every invocation channel until a file tool (read, edit, write) touches a matching path, and invoking a gated member from outside its gate hard-errors (`Unknown skill`) — the harness then tells the user it doesn't exist. So a skill that loads where its target cannot be invoked hands Claude an obligation it cannot act on. Two remedies: scope this skill's `paths` to the target's gate, or ungate the target. Advisory because containment is judged over sample paths each glob here matches, not decided, so a verdict can be wrong; retune or drop this clause in your own contract when it is. The judgment is over the gates, not over how they open: only a file tool (read, edit, write) opens a path gate — a shell read of a matching path, or a search tool's, opens none — so a session that works inside the gate through the shell alone loads neither member, and nothing static can see that.
